# Section 8 counterfactual (auto-generated by 23_counterfactual.py)

Counterfactual: each pair-window's observed slot (phase) error is removed while a, e, i, RAAN and argument of perigee keep their observed values -- the counterfactual distance is the nominal margin used throughout Sections 4-7, evaluated at the window centre (not re-propagated over the 24 h window; see the module docstring). Primary pair-windows only (on-grid, slowly drifting, standard angle).

| Period | Pair-windows | Observed events (rate, 95%) | Counterfactual events (rate, 95%) | Inherent (both) | Attributable (observed only) | Averted (counterfactual only) | Attributable share of observed events |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Overall | 1,576,868 | 1779 (1.13, 1.08-1.18) | 1932 (1.23, 1.17-1.28) | 653 | 1126 | 1279 | 63.3% (0.548-0.707) |
| Before April 2026 | 590,078 | 291 (0.493, 0.438-0.553) | 97 (0.164, 0.133-0.201) | 31 | 260 | 66 | 89.3% (0.784-0.987) |
| From April 2026 | 986,790 | 1488 (1.51, 1.43-1.59) | 1835 (1.86, 1.78-1.95) | 622 | 866 | 1213 | 58.2% (0.482-0.661) |

- Counterfactual/observed rate ratio: 1.086 (bootstrap 95% 0.884-1.29) -- close to 1 despite the per-window reshuffling, consistent with Section 6.4's finding that pair phase deviations show no net bias toward or away from alignment.
- 1126 of 1779 observed events (63.3%) occur at pair-windows whose nominal margin is >= 10 km: the observed phase deviation reduces the reconstructed separation sufficiently for the SGP4 screen to cross the 10 km threshold.
- 653 of 1779 observed events (36.7%) occur at pair-windows whose nominal margin is already < 10 km: the reconstructed nominal geometry places these pairs within the event threshold even after the observed phase deviation is removed.
- 1279 of 1932 counterfactual events (66.2%) are not observed events: at these pair-windows the observed phase deviation is associated with a larger separation than the centre-epoch nominal geometry alone implies.
- Attributable share before vs. from April 2026: 89.3% vs 58.2% -- the counterfactual (nominal-geometry-only) rate rose faster than the observed rate (0.164 to 1.86 per 1,000, a 11.3x increase, vs 0.493 to 1.51, a 3.1x increase). The decomposition therefore assigns a larger fraction of the 2026 rate increase to changes in reconstructed nominal geometry than to changes represented by the phase-deviation component. This is consistent with Section 7.5's finding that the rise is a composition effect associated with the P1-P6 nominal margin collapsing (RISE_TEST.md), not a change in how phase deviations behave (Section 6).
